title: "Choropleth maps in JavaScript with CanvasXpress"
description: "Color a world map by a value per country in the browser with CanvasXpress — join your data to a topoJSON by name and get an interactive, reproducible choropleth."
author: "Isaac Neuhaus"

---

A choropleth map shades each region by a value — emissions, population, votes, incidence. The
trick is always the same: join a table of values to a set of map shapes by a common key, then
pick a color scale. CanvasXpress does the join and the coloring inside the render, so in the
browser you pass one value per country and a topoJSON of boundaries and get an interactive,
reproducible figure.

## Load the library

```html
<link href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/neuhausi/canvasXpress@71.1.0/inst/htmlwidgets/lib/canvasXpress/canvasXpress.css" rel="stylesheet">
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/neuhausi/canvasXpress@71.1.0/inst/htmlwidgets/lib/canvasXpress/canvasXpress.min.js"></script>
```

## The markup and the spec

The **columns** (`smps`) are the countries — they match the map by name — and the single **row**
(`vars`) is the variable you color by: CO₂ emissions per country for 2018. We fetch a prepared
table and a small annotation table (continent, ISO code), parse the tab-separated text, and hand
the matrix to CanvasXpress. Swap the URL for any `country → value` table of your own.

```html
<canvas id="comap" width="700" height="500"></canvas>
<script>
  var DATA = "https://www.canvasxpress.org/data/r/cX-CO2-dat.txt";
  var SMP  = "https://www.canvasxpress.org/data/r/cX-CO2-smp.txt";

  // split a tab-separated file into a list of cell-arrays (one per row)
  function rows(text) {
    return text.trim().split("\n").map(function (line) { return line.split("\t"); });
  }

  Promise.all([fetch(DATA).then(function (r) { return r.text(); }),
               fetch(SMP ).then(function (r) { return r.text(); })])
    .then(function (texts) {
      var d = rows(texts[0]);                      // [header, ["CO2", v1, v2, ...]]
      var countries = d[0].slice(1);               // header, minus the empty corner cell
      var values    = d[1].slice(1).map(Number);   // the CO2 values

      var s = rows(texts[1]);                       // header + one row per country
      var col = {};                                 // header name -> column index
      s[0].forEach(function (name, i) { col[name] = i; });
      var byCountry = {};
      s.slice(1).forEach(function (r) { byCountry[r[0]] = r; });
      var continent = countries.map(function (c) { return byCountry[c][col["Continent"] + 1]; });

      var data = {
        y: { vars: ["CO2"], smps: countries, data: [values] },
        x: { Continent: continent }
      };
      var config = {
        graphType: "Map",
        colorBy: "CO2",
        topoJSON: "https://www.canvasxpress.org/data/maps/WORLD.json",
        mapId: "countries",
        legendPosition: "left",
        theme: "solarized",
        title: "CO2 Emissions per Country (2018)"
      };
      new CanvasXpress("comap", data, config);
    });
</script>
```

## Live result

```{=html}
<link href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/neuhausi/canvasXpress@71.1.0/inst/htmlwidgets/lib/canvasXpress/canvasXpress.css" rel="stylesheet">
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/neuhausi/canvasXpress@71.1.0/inst/htmlwidgets/lib/canvasXpress/canvasXpress.min.js"></script>
<canvas id="comapLive" width="700" height="500"></canvas>
<script>
(function () {
  var DATA = "https://www.canvasxpress.org/data/r/cX-CO2-dat.txt";
  var SMP  = "https://www.canvasxpress.org/data/r/cX-CO2-smp.txt";
  function rows(text) {
    return text.trim().split("\n").map(function (line) { return line.split("\t"); });
  }
  function draw() {
    if (typeof CanvasXpress === "undefined") { return setTimeout(draw, 60); }
    Promise.all([fetch(DATA).then(function (r) { return r.text(); }),
                 fetch(SMP ).then(function (r) { return r.text(); })])
      .then(function (texts) {
        var d = rows(texts[0]);
        var countries = d[0].slice(1);
        var values    = d[1].slice(1).map(Number);
        var s = rows(texts[1]);
        var col = {};
        s[0].forEach(function (name, i) { col[name] = i; });
        var byCountry = {};
        s.slice(1).forEach(function (r) { byCountry[r[0]] = r; });
        var continent = countries.map(function (c) { return byCountry[c][col["Continent"] + 1]; });
        new CanvasXpress("comapLive",
          { y: { vars: ["CO2"], smps: countries, data: [values] }, x: { Continent: continent } },
          { graphType: "Map", colorBy: "CO2",
            topoJSON: "https://www.canvasxpress.org/data/maps/WORLD.json",
            mapId: "countries", legendPosition: "left", theme: "solarized",
            title: "CO2 Emissions per Country (2018)" });
      });
  }
  draw();
})();
</script>
```

Each country is shaded by its emissions, the legend maps color to value, and hovering a country
shows its name, continent and number. The whole figure is one portable spec — data, boundaries
and color rule together — that you can re-render from R or Python.

## Beyond the world map

Point `topoJSON` at a different boundary file to map US states, a single country's provinces, or
a custom region — the join key is just the shape name. Switch `colorBy` to a categorical field
for a qualitative map, add `decorations` to drop labeled markers on cities, or set
`mapProjection` for an Albers or Mercator view.
